speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I would first like to record my appreciation to the Singapore city planners and the MND planning team that have really allowed Singapore's reputation as a City in a Garden to flourish in the minds of so many who look to our city for urban planning ideas.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Motion is meant to support that vision of Singapore being a City in a Garden and, by extension, being a place where people live around lush greenery, nature and wildlife.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is with such a spirit that I wish to deliver this speech.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have looked very carefully at the Environmental Baseline Study which I must thank MND and HDB for so openly sharing with the public.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But if one looks at the study, you will see vast numbers of plant and animal species, including species that are critically endangered.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This has caused me some concern if we were to demolish the forest.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Now, this forest is also	between Ghim Moh,	Mount Sinai, Pine Grove and Holland Grove estates.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, it is not just a forest but a shared and extended green landscape that the residents have, for a long time, admired and grown used to.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Ulu Pandan residents know that I have a record of both developing the land in Ulu Pandan to make the best use of it but also, where possible, to preserve an environment of greenery to surround their estates.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: When Ghim Moh Link was being built some years ago, I walked the ground along the canal and worked together with different agencies to get signs hammered into the ground to state "protected tree".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It would be too easy to just say "halt and do not demolish Dover Forest" without giving alternatives.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, in the spirit of partnership and transparency, I would like to share with URA and MND some possible alternative sites and, in so doing, also share the long-term aspiration for Ulu Pandan and how this fits in.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have given a significant amount of time thinking about how to preserve as much of the forest as possible.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One way to achieve this is through the use of vacant sites.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In considering possible alternative locations for the development of BTOs, I would like to propose the vacant plot of land next to the Ulu Pandan CC.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That, to me, is a golden opportunity to have a serious rethink about how we can grow, enhance and rejuvenate Ghim Moh Town.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My idea is to use the 4.6 and the 4.9 gross plot ratio sites as BTO plots as well as possible SERS plots in rejuvenating some of the older blocks in Ghim Moh.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I can appreciate that SERS is a sensitive topic.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Although I am not expecting an answer today, given its sensitivity, I would like to put on record that my long-term aspiration, which I have given a fair amount of time thinking about, includes both an influx of BTO flats and also the rejuvenation of Ghim Moh for the existing residents living there.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: When Ghim Moh Link was built some years ago, the residents from the old Blocks 9 to 12A, through SERS, moved to Ghim Moh Link and the old blocks were demolished.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That land which the old blocks stood on, is now the vacant plot of land beside Ulu Pandan CC.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This vacant plot of land opens the door to unprecedented possibilities of how we may use the land in as creative a way as possible.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, when I say that the two plots completely vacant now can be used for both BTO as well as, subject to MND's clearance, for SERS, I do not say that in a flippant manner.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One such group of flats is a group of six blocks of 3-room flats on the other side of the Ulu Pandan CC.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I ask that the gross plot ratio be reconsidered so as to increase it.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There could be a selective en bloc of these six blocks to the vacant plot of land next to the CC.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This then will release the whole plot where these Blocks 1 to 6 currently sit on, thereby releasing another jigsaw piece, another plot of land, for my other residents who are living around Ghim Moh market, that is, in Blocks 7 to 21, to be rehoused into that vacant plot of land, possibly through SERS.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The vision is to continue to keep the market as the heart of Ghim Moh while, at the same time, rejuvenating the whole of Ghim Moh town through a deliberate and phased SERS development and the use of high gross plot ratios.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The land around the market can then be redeveloped for more and taller housing, if my idea of offering SERS to Blocks 1 to 21 is accepted by MND.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This will mean the ability to accommodate new residents in BTO flats as well as provide new flats with new leases for existing Ghim Moh residents, through SERS.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is my suggestion as an alternative, instead of felling Dover Forest.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: One constraint that MND may tell me today in response is that the pieces of land I have in mind are insufficient to accommodate BTO and SERS flats.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My response, if I may, to that point is that there are two other under-utilised plots of land in Ghim Moh that we can use for planning purposes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The first is MOE's Language Centre, which was the old, now defunct, Ghim Moh Primary School.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Residents of Mount Sinai, as well as residents of Ghim Moh, would know that there is a huge old unused field there lying fallow.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, that also allows for space for additional housing.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If MND's view is that this is still insufficient land, although I do not think it is insufficient, but if MND is of the view that it is still insufficient, I have an additional solution to propose.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This involves questioning whether or not we need the old sprawling RJC campus to remain.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, it is not housing any school now and its fields are unused.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: According to the Master Plan, the campus is subject to detailed planning.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such a holistic rejuvenation of Ghim Moh Town will allow it to flow seamlessly into Holland Village with the rail corridor being the natural green valley between the two towns.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, one can picture that – a rejuvenated Ghim Moh with a green valley being the rail corridor seamlessly linking on to Holland Village and that town.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I believe in providing alternative plans and solutions within my own constituency.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, when the former Nexus International School campus was transformed into a temporary dormitory to house essential migrant workers in June 2020, we welcomed these workers in Ulu Pandan.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the end, it worked out to the benefit of everyone.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It also built mutual trust and respect between residents and workers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We – the residents of Ulu Pandan and I – did not take a NIMBY approach to the workers and have welcomed them to the Nexus site.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, we were discussing that it being called the Nexus International School, how wonderful it would be if, after our essential workers came in and occupied the dormitory, there will be a nexus created between the workers and the residents.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And I dare say there has been, fortunately.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, the point that I am making is, if more BTO flats need to be built, we have a solution in Ulu Pandan.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This allows for a compact community allowing for the inflow of new residents to live alongside existing Ghim Moh residents.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some of the new residents will be the children of existing Ghim Moh families who will be able to buy BTO flats next to their parents.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But this idea of conservation and having residents live within a green environment surrounded by greenery and nature is not something that has been crystalised by virtue of what we are debating today.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This has been my long-term aspiration for Ulu Pandan residents I serve.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Allow me now, Sir, to expand on this long-term aspiration as it foretells or provides insight into why the Motion was worded as "Preservation of Dover Forest in Ulu Pandan".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It was worded such because it is part of a wider aspiration for residents and it is not constrained to residents living in Ghim Moh.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If you can picture it from a satellite view, if we were to retain Dover Forest, it would mean that we have a wonderful loop of nature around the whole constituency.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Dover Forest links up all the way to Clementi Road, where if you cross Clementi Road, the Ulu Pandan park connector runs along and links up to my residents in Sunset Way.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And there is a railway bridge that connects to an expanse of green land that goes behind the Sunset Way HDB estate and eventually leads to Clementi Forest, which then eventually leads out to the Rail Corridor and Bukit Timah Railway Station.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If one comes back down the Rail Corridor and Bukit Timah Railway Station heading south, you will go through the estates of Old Holland, Greenleaf, Mount Sinai and then back to Ghim Moh.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, a loop of greenery within Ulu Pandan itself.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And there are other estates within Ulu Pandan that will be able to link up to the Rail Corridor, especially through the Holland Green Linear Park, which we recently opened.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, for residents living in Namly Estate and Coronation Estate, all they have to do is cross Sixth Avenue, walk down Laurel Wood Avenue and they will get to Holland Plain which will link up eventually to the Rail Corridor.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My hope is that we will be able to have a footpath that connects Holland Green Linear Park to Clementi Road through the scenic route of Clementi Forest which, I should state, I would like preserved, where possible.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, there is a whole belt of condos along Bukit Timah Road that will be able to link up to the Rail Corridor, through the sky walk above Bukit Timah Canal as part of the Bukit Timah-Rochor Green Corridor Initiative.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, if you can picture a satellite’s view, that would mean everyone living in between King Albert Park and Sixth Avenue, both condo-dwellers and house-dwellers, will be able to walk down, connect to Bukit Timah Railway Station, link to the Rail Corridor, head south, head to Ghim Moh and down to Dover Forest.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, Mr Speaker, the idea is to have Ulu Pandan residents live within a landscape of lush greenery.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This aspiration for the constituency I serve, especially the phased rejuvenation of major towns, will take 20 years or more from today – very likely, beyond my time as a Member of Parliament in this House.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But that should not stop me from aspiring for my residents today.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A 40-year-old forest is home to creatures over many life cycles.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Many life cycles of creatures and species create an eco-system.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Mr de Souza shared that the Ulu Pandan site, which some refer to as the “Dover Forest”, is close to the hearts of his residents and he spoke up very passionately about this topic.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: As someone who grew up in the area and spent much time exploring the spaces there, I can well appreciate these sentiments, and the way that Mr de Souza described the regions that he has in Ulu Pandan gives me a tinge of regret for moving out.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Ulu Pandan site used to be a rubber plantation before it was abandoned.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It was re-zoned for residential use under the Master Plan 2003.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We were mindful of this characteristic when planning for its development.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Hence, the HDB engaged a consultant to conduct an environmental baseline study to inform our plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Nature groups were consulted and many residents living in the area provided feedback when the report was published online and we received a wide range of views.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Some called for the preservation of the Ulu Pandan site and asked HDB to consider alternative sites in the area instead, and Mr de Souza mentioned a number of these sites in his speech.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Others supported using the site for public housing so as to meet the needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: However, these respondents also called for the site to be developed in a way that allows for their children and their grandchildren to continue enjoying the greenery.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We are studying the feedback and welcome more Singaporeans to provide their views as we refine plans for the Ulu Pandan site.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will carefully consider the feedback received and share our plans when ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We take this approach of consulting stakeholders and balancing the different needs of Singaporeans seriously.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Minister Desmond Lee spoke about this important stewardship role earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Because land is scarce in Singapore, we have to plan judiciously.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We recycle our limited land, for instance, through selling it on a leasehold basis, allowing us to refresh our land use and renew our cityscape and neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We optimise our limited land supply by co-locating uses, increasing the density of land plots, redeveloping existing sites and, where it makes sense, going underground.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For example, the East Coast Integrated Depot, will incorporate three MRT depots and one for buses.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: With careful planning, we can safeguard some of our ecologically important sites as green spaces, such as the Kranji Marshes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And where we have to develop greenfield sites, we do so after careful deliberation, seeking to preserve and integrate natural elements into the developments.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: At the heart of these decisions, it is not just about balancing the various needs of Singaporeans today, but, importantly, it is also about balancing the needs of today’s generation with those that come after us.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And that is why I am very heartened that despite the differing viewpoints we received on the Ulu Pandan site, there was a common thread running through the feedback: there was a strong desire to be responsible stewards for future generations.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: And we put in just as much thought and effort into conserving nature.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is part of our DNA, deeply intertwined with our Singapore Story.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The lush greenery we see today is the result of dedicated and sustained efforts by generations of Singaporeans who have been greening our city and planting trees year after year for over 60 years.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is the result of deliberate decisions made by earlier terms of Government, who have safeguarded our green spaces even as they developed our urban landscape and built homes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We have a vision to transform Singapore into a City in Nature.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to identify core biodiversity areas and their surrounding buffers, and retain these sites where possible.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will also continue to strengthen ecological connectivity through enhancing our network of ecological corridors, such as the Bukit Batok Nature Corridor.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: These efforts will help us mitigate the impact of urbanisation and climate change and provide a high-quality living environment for Singaporeans, with greater access to nature’s benefits.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: (In Mandarin):    Mr Speaker, Sir, I can understand the concerns and wishes of Mr de Souza’s residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: The Ulu Pandan site which some referred to as “Dover Forest”, was rezoned for residential use as part of the Master Plan 2003.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: HDB engaged a consultant to conduct an Environmental Baseline Study before it proceeded with its planning.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We received a wide range of views from different groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Some called for the preservation of the Ulu Pandan site, while others supported using the site for public housing to meet the needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: For those who supported the development of the site, they called for it to be developed in a way that allows for their children and grandchildren to continue enjoying the greenery.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We welcome more Singaporeans to give their views and inputs, as we consider our plans for the Ulu Pandan site.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will carefully consider all the feedback received and share our plans when ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We take this approach of consulting stakeholders and balancing the different needs of Singaporeans seriously.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: Because land is scarce in Singapore, we have to plan judiciously.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: It is not just about balancing the various needs of Singaporeans today but, importantly, it is also about balancing the needs of today’s generation with those that come after us.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We put in just as much thought and effort into conserving nature.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: We will continue to consult and engage with Singaporeans, consider their feedback and suggestions seriously as we balance the various needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Tan Kiat How)
text: I am confident that we can do so if all Singaporeans continue to see ourselves as stewards for what we have and for the future.
